title: Client Intake Statement
text: Client reports she slipped on clear liquid detergent in aisle 7 of a Highland Market store on February 4, 2026. She fell directly onto her right side and felt immediate right knee pain and low back pain. She states there were no warning cones in place before the fall. Client denies any prior right knee treatment and reports missing several warehouse shifts after the incident.

title: Store Incident Report
text: Internal incident report notes that a customer slipped near aisle 7 where a clear detergent spill was observed after the fall. The report states no floor warning cone had been placed before the incident and that cleanup was initiated only after plaintiff was assisted from the ground.

title: Urgent Care Evaluation
text: Patient presents same day after slip-and-fall with right knee pain, swelling, and low back pain. Exam notes antalgic gait and reduced weight-bearing tolerance. X-ray negative for fracture. Diagnosed with right knee sprain and lumbar strain. Provider issued brace, work excuse, anti-inflammatory medication, and orthopedic referral.

title: Orthopedic Knee Evaluation
text: Plaintiff evaluated for persistent right knee instability, swelling, and lumbar pain after the store fall. Exam shows positive McMurray testing, joint line tenderness, and guarded squat mechanics. Physician suspects medial meniscus injury, orders right knee MRI, starts physical therapy, and removes plaintiff from work for two weeks.

title: Right Knee MRI Findings
text: MRI of the right knee demonstrates a probable posterior horn medial meniscus tear with small joint effusion. Impression recommends orthopedic surgical consultation if instability persists and continuation of physical therapy for mobility and pain control.

title: Physical Therapy Evaluation
text: Initial therapy evaluation shows reduced right knee flexion, painful stairs, guarded gait, and reduced lifting tolerance. Lower Extremity Functional Scale documents 41 percent disability. Therapist recommends ten visits over five weeks focused on gait restoration, strength, and swelling control.

title: Employer Wage Verification
text: Employer confirms plaintiff missed 56 work hours between February 5 and February 18, 2026 because of injury-related restrictions. Average hourly wage at the time was 24.50 dollars.

title: Current Medical Billing Ledger
text: Current medical billing ledger reflects urgent care charges of 980 dollars, orthopedic charges of 875 dollars, MRI charges of 1850 dollars, physical therapy charges of 720 dollars, and pharmacy charges of 95 dollars. No surgical consultation or procedure charges have been added yet.
